body.statement: For every \(\Sigma_*\in C\) and fixed \(h>0\), the alternatives \(\Sigma_n^{-}\) and \(\Sigma_n^{+}\) lie in \(U\cap\mathcal K\) for all large \(n\), satisfy \(\mathcal P(\Sigma_n^{-})=\{-1\}\) and \(\mathcal P(\Sigma_n^{+})=\{-1,+1\}\), and have \(\operatorname{dist}(\Sigma_n^{-},K_{+1})\asymp n^{-1/2}\). Their \(n\)-snapshot Gaussian experiments are mutually contiguous, uniformly for \(\Sigma_*\) on compact contact subcharts. Consequently, any procedure \(\widetilde\Gamma_n\) satisfying asymptotic uniform coverage of \(\mathcal P\) at level \(1-\alpha\) has \(\liminf\Pr_{\Sigma_n^{-}}\{+1\in\widetilde\Gamma_n\}>0\) along these sequences and cannot recover the singleton uniformly at root-\(n\) contact distance.
body.justification: The lower bound shows that the clearance rate in the upper theorem is locally sharp for honest procedures.
body.gap: Kaji2021 gives general weak-identification impossibility, but the reduced-form coordinate, contact geometry, and Gaussian covariance divergence are new to this OU target.
body.consumer: The result prevents claims of uniformly faster singleton classification and identifies the appropriate reporting regime near contact.
body.proof_tex:
Write \(\epsilon_n=h/\sqrt n\).  Along the fixed \(t\)-direction, the exact quadratic expansion at a contact point is
\[
 g(\Sigma_*\pm\epsilon_n H)
 =\pm g_t(\Sigma_*)\epsilon_n+2\eta(s_*+u_*)\epsilon_n^2. \tag{25}
\]
Since \(g_t>0\) on the compact contact subchart, (25) is negative for the minus alternative and positive for the plus alternative for all sufficiently large \(n\), uniformly on that subchart.  Both alternatives converge uniformly to \(C\), so they lie in \(U\cap\mathcal K\).  The asymmetric-contact theorem then gives their two asserted polarity sets.  Equation (25) and the local-contact-geometry theorem give constants \(0<c_h<C_h<\infty\) such that
\[
 c_hn^{-1/2}\le\operatorname{dist}(\Sigma_n^-,K_{+1})
 \le C_hn^{-1/2}. \tag{26}
\]

We next prove mutual contiguity directly.  For one observation let \(P=\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_n^-)\), \(Q=\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_n^+)\), and
\[
 B=(\Sigma_n^-)^{-1/2}\Sigma_n^+(\Sigma_n^-)^{-1/2}=I+E.
\]
Uniform positive definiteness on the compact neighborhood gives \(\lVert E\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le Cn^{-1/2}\).  For large \(n\), \(\lVert E\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}<1\).  Whitening under \(P\) and evaluating the elementary Gaussian integral yields
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_P\left(\frac{dQ}{dP}\right)^2
 &=\det(B)^{-1}\det(2B^{-1}-I)^{-1/2}\\
 &=\det\{I-(B-I)^2\}^{-1/2}
 =\det(I-E^2)^{-1/2}.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{27}
\end{equation}
If \(e_1,e_2\) are the eigenvalues of \(E\), then \(-\log(1-e_j^2)\le2e_j^2\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Therefore the second moment for the \(n\)-fold product is bounded by
\[
 \left[\det(I-E^2)^{-1/2}\right]^n
 \le\exp\{n\lVert E\rVert_F^2\}\le C_0<\infty, \tag{28}
\]
uniformly on the compact subchart.  Interchanging \(\Sigma_n^-\) and \(\Sigma_n^+\) gives the same bound in the reverse direction.  For any events \(A_n\), Cauchy--Schwarz and (28) give
\[
 Q_n(A_n)\le C_0^{1/2}P_n(A_n)^{1/2},
 \]
and the reverse inequality with the roles exchanged.  This is mutual contiguity.

Finally let \(A_n=\{+1\in\widetilde\Gamma_n\}\).  Asymptotic uniform coverage at level \(1-\alpha\), applied to \(\Sigma_n^+\) whose true set contains \(+1\), gives \(\liminf Q_n(A_n)\ge1-\alpha\).  The preceding second-moment inequality then yields
\[
 \liminf P_n(A_n)\ge\frac{(1-\alpha)^2}{C_0}>0. \tag{29}
\]
At \(\Sigma_n^-\) the true set is \(\{-1\}\), so (29) prevents the probability of returning that singleton from tending to one uniformly at the distance in (26).  This proves the claimed root-\(n\) obstruction.
